A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-Mem work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures and prompts, support reliable comparison despite relocated references and renumbered sections.

before.justification: v4 reports original A-EQA, EM-EQA and GOAT-Bench evaluations, ablations and qualitative failure analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds full-set evaluations, frontier-component ablations and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The co-visibility clustering algorithm, incremental memory construction, frontier snapshots, prefiltering, navigation procedure and VLM training objectives are unchanged. The newly evaluated variants are ablation controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use A-EQA, EM-EQA and GOAT-Bench with the same underlying domains and question-answering and multimodal navigation tasks. Full-set evaluation increases sample counts within retained benchmarks; it does not introduce a distinct task or environment scenario.

E2.justification: The baseline sets in Tables 1–5 are unchanged. New Table 7 adds nearest-frontier comparison variants labeled SnapMem w/o FS and SnapMem w/o FS & Mem. Its full SnapMem row matches the existing 3D-Mem results.

E3.justification: Appendix 6 adds full-set evaluation alongside the original subsets. New experiments introduce nearest-frontier controls and component latency measurement. Section 4.1 also revises the stated LLM-Match mapping from 20–100 to 0–100, without establishing that the unchanged existing scores were recomputed.

E4.justification: v5 adds direct tests of the central frontier-selection component: nearest-frontier navigation on both benchmarks and joint removal of frontier snapshots and memory maintenance on GOAT-Bench (Appendix 13.2, Table 7). Together with the new component latency analysis in Table 6, these substantially extend mechanism and efficiency validation beyond the retained memory, decision-frequency and hyperparameter analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new tables retain point-value reporting, and the existing plots' reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing tables and result curves retain their values. Appendix 6 adds full-set A-EQA LLM-Match/LLM-Match SPL of 53.3/38.0 and GOAT-Bench success rate/SPL of 62.9/44.7. Table 7 adds nearest-frontier results of 49.3/31.0 and 63.7/46.8, respectively, plus GOAT-Bench 57.2/33.2 without memory maintenance. Table 6 adds component timings. These materially broaden the findings; the full-set scores are additional results under different sampling, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 revises the stated normalization range of LLM-Match from 20–100 to 0–100, a limited change to the metric's mathematical specification. The snapshot definitions, update equations, clustering termination argument and other mathematical content remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: compact visual scene memory, frontier-based exploration, incremental construction and retrieval supporting lifelong tasks, and effectiveness on three benchmarks. The wording edits and additional evidence do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix 7.3 explicitly discusses static-environment applicability, moving objects, long-term pose accuracy and inference latency with possible mitigations. Appendix 13.2 explains the frontier-ablation behavior through retained lifelong memory and states why removing prefiltering would exceed VLM context limits. Earlier detector and VLM failure interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Table 6 newly discloses component runtimes, including VLM inference times of 3.34 seconds on A-EQA and 3.58 seconds on GOAT-Bench. The project-page address also changes. Existing implementation hyperparameters, training and hardware disclosures, and complete prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes some criticisms concerning dense representations' spatial information and reasoning methods' dependence on fully observed scenes. Its new topological-mapping paragraph summarizes material already present in v4's appendix. TSGM and RoboHop were already cited, and the removed duplicate 3D-LLM bibliography entry is not a distinct lost work.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized prose and section-title edits, reformats the author affiliations, adds contact information and introduces several appendix headings. References move behind the appendices, but most narrative and technical text retains its wording and order.

P2.justification: v5 adds two unnumbered full-set summary tables, latency Table 6 and ablation Table 7. Tables 1 and 3 gain subset-identification markers and caption explanations. Existing numbered figures are retained with limited resizing and relocation, and the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: v5 strengthens the existing paper through full-set performance checks, direct frontier-component controls, measured latency and clearer applicability limits. The gains are bounded: full-set results cover only 3D-Mem, while the main comparative evidence and method remain unchanged. New editorial defects, including the unresolved Table ?? reference and unexplained SnapMem labeling, slightly reduce polish but do not outweigh the added evidence and transparency.
